interface.title: PlateMaster - Dashboard for Plate Analysis (v1.3.0)
interface.field: Plate-reader assays in cell and molecular biology and biochemistry: 96-well absorbance or fluorescence time courses
interface.stage_of_work: Analysis and reporting after data collection: import, quality check, grouping, statistics, plotting and export
interface.what_it_is_for: Load a batch of plate-reader Excel files (one per time point), check how they were read, group wells into conditions with a plate-map template, aggregate and optionally filter outliers, run descriptive statistics and Welch t-tests, plot time courses with error bars, and export everything as an Excel report.

data.note: Uploaded the five validation_plate_{0,5,10,15,20}.xlsx files through 'Local PC upload'. The app took the time point from the last number in each file name. On the first pass, grouping came from plate_map.csv. An accidental page reload reset the session, so the files were loaded again and analysis_settings.json was imported to restore the template groups and settings. Results with the template and Mean aggregation: Control = 4.5, 5.5, 6.5, 7.5, 8.5 and Treatment_11 = 26.5, 29.5, 32.5, 35.5, 38.5 at t = 0, 5, 10, 15, 20. The imported settings preset a Welch test of Control at t0 against Treatment_11 at t20: t = -27.76, df ≈ 14, p = 1.2e-13. Control against Treatment_11, both at t20: t = -24.49, p = 6.8e-13. The browser could not open the expected_*.csv files. A reviewer later checked them and confirmed that these group means, and the Control t0 vs Treatment_11 t20 Welch result (t = -27.7609, df 14, p = 1.215e-13), match expected_group_results.csv and expected_welch_comparison.csv exactly.

ZIP upload: no ZIP file among the test files
Named presets (Save preset now / Load preset / Apply preset): seen but not tried within the action budget
IQR and MAD outlier methods and their parameter controls: listed in the Method dropdown, but only Z-score was run
'By original rows' aggregation layout, the Rows/Columns subset pickers, and Aggregation functions other than Mean (Median, Min, Max, Std, Sum): seen but not changed from the defaults

not_done: The explorer did not compare results against expected_group_results.csv and expected_welch_comparison.csv, because the browser can only upload these files, not open them. A reviewer later confirmed an exact match for Control 4.5–8.5, Treatment_11 26.5–38.5 over t = 0–20, and Welch t = -27.7609, df 14, p = 1.215e-13 (Control t0 vs Treatment_11 t20). The t20-vs-t20 result (t = -24.49) was not among the checked values.
Could not read the contents of plate_master_report.xlsx: the download reader only reports the size of binary files (24,329 bytes), so its sheets were not checked.
A browser navigation part-way through reset the Streamlit session, so files and settings had to be loaded again (the second pass used analysis_settings.json).

The explorer's Download settings.json click has no screenshot showing the download. In the replay, the first click on Download settings.json did nothing and the second downloaded plate_master_analysis.json.

Possible issues seen: (1) The 'Clear all' × on the cross-file series picker did nothing; the list came straight back full (screens/053.webp), so chips had to be removed one at a time. (2) With Bar plot by Time, no error bars were drawn under 95% CI or SEM. The code confirms this is by design: the bar branches (PlateMaster1.2.py:1483–1508) add no error-bar layer, and only the line chart does. The Error bar method control still appears for these plot types. (3) Suspected app bug: with Z-score at 1.00, Outlier statistics reported 240/480 removed overall and 48/96 per time point, but 0 removed for every group, even though the removed-values table lists Control wells (A1, B1, G1, H1). (4) The replay saw the Time legend of the bar chart sort as text (0, 10, 15, 20, 5).

Not tried within the ~100-action budget: Color scale mode, Color palette, the Rows/Columns subset selectors, the aggregation functions other than Mean, the table toolbar buttons (show/hide columns, CSV download, search, fullscreen), and the chart's PNG/Vega-spec export.
